clue.text: Recommend writing about odd characters in plot

indicators.note: about means the writing goes round the other letters

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word plot are taken, first and third

explanation.surface: Someone advises on a story that needs some strange characters written into its plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose something is to put it forward as a suggestion, much as you would recommend it.

clue.text: Ferret cut farmer's production in field

parts.note: to ferret is to root about or search
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A ferret, its hair trimmed, scampers across a field where the farmer grows things.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips, beet and potatoes are vegetables grown underground in fields, the produce of arable farming.

clue.text: Easy profits from ruler seen in photos

indicators.note: seen in means the ruler's word appears inside the photos' word

parts.note: pics is a casual word for photographs
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A tabloid makes a quick fortune from pictures of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains made with little effort are called rich or easy pickings, an idiom for profits.

clue.text: Well, bread is a possible starter in restaurant

parts.note: a spring is a natural well of water
a roll is a small piece of bread

explanation.surface: A diner muses that bread might do as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' reads as a conversational opener, but it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: This fried pastry parcel is a typical appetiser in Chinese restaurants, hence a possible first course.

clue.text: Slight speech defect

definitions.meaning: slurred speech runs the sounds together indistinctly

explanation.surface: A minor impairment in how someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an insulting remark and indistinct pronunciation, two separate senses.

clue.text: Move to employ one Australian flier

indicators.note: to employ is to take in, so the moving word takes in the letter for one

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pilot from Australia is being headhunted to relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small parrot native to Australia, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Issue could be treason, having killed leader

indicators.note: killing the leader removes the first letter of the treason word

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: A political issue: would assassinating the head of state count as treason?
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper or magazine issue is one printing of it, a particular version.

clue.text: Angry, upset about a right sort of loaf

indicators.note: about means the mixed letters go round the other pair
upset means the letters of angry are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being served the correct kind of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf of this kind is brown bread made with malted wheat flakes, a type of bread.

clue.text: Struggle helplessly seeing line adopted by father

indicators.note: adopted by means the line's letter is taken into the father's word

parts.note: the founder of a movement is called its father

explanation.surface: A child struggles on seeing a line drawn by their dad.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to thrash about or blunder without making progress, as in mud or water.

clue.text: Business worry

definitions.meaning: a firm or company is a going ...

explanation.surface: Two words: commerce and anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commercial firm and a feeling of anxiety, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Bachelor's first trendy place by the sea

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word bachelor is used

parts.note: right-on means fashionably progressive

explanation.surface: A single man's first fashionable seaside haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a resort on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: This English town on the Sussex coast is a famous seaside resort.

clue.text: Attack and do as ordered, beset by girl getting married

indicators.note: beset by means the shuffled letters are surrounded by the married girl's word

parts.note: a bride is a woman at her wedding

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of do as are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bride is told to do as she is told and lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do as ordered' reads as obedience, but 'ordered' rearranges DO AS into OADS, which BRIDE surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal onslaught, originally a volley from all a ship's guns on one side.

clue.text: First part of a play with number going round fighting

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a play

indicators.note: going round means the number's letters turn back to front

explanation.surface: The opening act of a drama features a song and a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers seeing action are engaged in combat, so the word stands for fighting.

clue.text: Opportunity backed after complaint — game might be raised here here

indicators.note: after puts the backed word behind the complaint

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble

indicators.note: backed means the opportunity word runs backwards

parts.note: room, as in room for improvement, is scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A grievance is backed, and game birds are reared on this land.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'here' twice, a slip; the second is ignored. A grouse moor is upland heath in Britain kept for shooting the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse, a game bird, are bred and shot on such moorland, so the game is raised there.

clue.text: Wake selected pupils after mistake

indicators.note: after puts the pupils' word behind the mistake

parts.note: a slip is a small error
a stream is a group of pupils grouped by ability

explanation.surface: Children in a top set wake up after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for the trail behind a moving vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The current of air or water behind a fast-moving object is its wake or slipstream.

clue.text: Marathon record broken by nationalist's leader

indicators.note: broken by means the record's word is split by the other letter

parts.note: a log is a written record

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word nationalist

explanation.surface: A long-distance running record falls to a separatist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon session is a lengthy one, so the word is used adjectivally here as lengthy.

clue.text: Son's promise in front of mainly suspicious swimmer

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for son
giving your word is making a promise

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: fishy means dubious or suspicious

explanation.surface: A son swears loyalty despite being somewhat distrustful.
explanation.definitionFit: This large ocean fish with a long pointed bill is a swimmer in the playful crossword sense.

clue.text: Area covered by recasting of Hot Lips in MASH?

indicators.note: covered by means the area letter is surrounded by the mixed letters
recasting means the letters of hot lips are cast into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recast of the TV show M*A*S*H, whose character Hot Lips is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot Lips Houlihan is the head nurse in the US TV series M*A*S*H.
explanation.definitionFit: MASH stands for Mobile Army Surgical Hospital, so one is a military medical unit.

clue.text: Clear instruction from Pope on sleep

parts.note: a papal bull is a formal decree from the Pope
to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: The Pope issues a clear edict about napping.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze land is to clear it with a heavy earth-moving vehicle.

clue.text: Discourage work on fourth estate

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
the fourth estate is a name for the press

explanation.surface: Pressure on journalists hampers their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh heavily on someone's spirits is to dishearten or depress them, a sense close to discourage.

clue.text: Weapon hurt one of Macron's

parts.note: stung means hurt, as by an insult or a bee
un is French for one, the French president Macron's language

explanation.surface: A weapon injured one of the French president's people.
explanation.definitionFit: An electroshock device that immobilises a person is a non-lethal weapon.

clue.text: Duty of old star from the east

indicators.note: from the east means read right to left in an across answer, so backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: The obligation of an ageing celebrity from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, the duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Top bill and see off large corporations

indicators.note: off means the letters go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Headline a bill and fend off big business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jocular British word for a big belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporation in the old jokey sense is a paunch, so big ones are paunches.

clue.text: Tagine must be cooked for this purpose

definitions.text: Tagine must be cooked for this purpose

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of tagine are mixed into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Moroccan stew has to be cooked so it can be consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a tagine is cooked so that it can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is cooked for consumption, which is the purpose the clue points to.

clue.text: Drink connection keeping pupils regularly missing

indicators.note: keeping means the connection holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a tie is a link or connection

indicators.note: regularly missing means every other letter of pupils is dropped, leaving the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A link between drinking and pupils who often skip school.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, someone's usual tipple being their favourite.

clue.text: Mobile resonating as missing such a noise

indicators.note: mobile means the letters are free to move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mobile phone resonates, its distinctive sound missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' says the letters of 'as' are taken out of the anagram of RESONATING. 'such a noise' refers back to 'Mobile', which doubles as the definition's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone plays a tune or tone to announce an incoming call.

clue.text: Christmas will be held up by little ones

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means carried within, so the letters sit inside the words little ones

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Christmas will be delayed by the children.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'will be' into the definition; it is a link joining definition to wordplay, so the definition is 'Christmas' alone. In a down answer, held up reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is the French-derived word for the festive season, used in carols.

clue.text: France is French — nothing about garnish

parts.note: F is the international code for France
est is French for is
O is zero, nothing
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: France is French, and nothing more to say about its decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To festoon is to decorate with chains of flowers or ribbons, adorning as a garnish does.

clue.text: Blow chances finally getting question with queen

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of chances

parts.note: and means together with
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone wastes their opportunities when asked something by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow money is to waste it, the same as frittering it away.

clue.text: Suggests Independent politician is economical with the truth!

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
a jocular phrase for lies

explanation.surface: An independent MP is being less than truthful, it is hinted.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply something is to hint at it without saying it outright.
